gen_risks.description: Delay in Final Investment Decision could push construction start and commissioning, reducing value for money.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement a firm FID decision timetable, accelerate procurement, and include schedule contingency in contract milestones.
gen_risks.evidence: Option 2: Padeswood Delayed... resulting in a subsequent 5‑month delay to COD (section 3.1)

gen_risks.description: Revenue support under the ICC Contract may be reduced or delayed, threatening cash‑flow.
gen_risks.mitigation: Negotiate a legally binding RSA with clear payment triggers and include performance guarantees or escrow arrangements.
gen_risks.evidence: Revenue Support Agreement (RSA) listed under Financial Risks (section 5.4.1)

gen_risks.description: Project could be discontinued after FID, leading to sunk costs and loss of strategic benefits.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish staged go/no‑go gates with independent review, maintain contingency reserve, and secure commitment letters from key stakeholders.

gen_risks.description: Potential shortfall in Exchequer funding or changes to SoSDA agreements could create financing gaps.
gen_risks.mitigation: Obtain multi‑year funding commitments via SoSDA, diversify financing with private equity, and include funding contingency in cash flow model.
gen_risks.evidence: Exchequer funding Secretary of State direct agreements (SoSDA) (section 5.4.3)

gen_risks.description: Fraudulent claims or misuse of grant funds could erode project budget and reputation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply rigorous procurement procedures, regular internal audits, and independent fraud monitoring by DESNZ CGL.

gen_risks.description: CCS technology may not achieve capture performance at the required scale, jeopardising emissions targets.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct detailed engineering design reviews, pilot subsystem testing, and retain WSP technical oversight throughout construction.
gen_risks.evidence: first at‑scale UK cement plant incorporating CCS technology (section 1)

gen_risks.description: Integration between capture plant and CO₂ transport/storage network may encounter cross‑chain interface failures.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop detailed interface control documents, joint integration team, and schedule buffers for transport‑storage handover.

gen_risks.description: Changes to the CCS Network Code or related legislation could render current contracts non‑compliant.
gen_risks.mitigation: Monitor regulatory developments, embed change‑in‑law clauses, and maintain liaison with Ofgem and network code authority.
gen_risks.evidence: Padeswood is compliant with the CCS Network Code (section 4.6)

gen_risks.description: Rising carbon price and the introduction of CBAM may affect the economic case and competitiveness of UK cement.
gen_risks.mitigation: Secure long‑term revenue support via ICC contract, model scenarios with carbon price floors, and engage in CBAM policy consultations.
gen_risks.evidence: rising carbon price, impacting competitiveness with imports; CBAM will be introduced in 2027 (section 2.1.3)

gen_risks.description: Coordination among multiple oversight bodies could cause decision delays or misaligned actions.
gen_risks.mitigation: Create a governance charter defining roles, hold weekly coordination meetings, and use a shared project management platform.
gen_risks.evidence: oversight through a range of bodies including Ofgem, LCCC, DESNZ CGL, DESNZ Cluster Function Team (section 4.5)

gen_risks.description: Potential CO₂ leakage from storage could lead to environmental damage and regulatory penalties.
gen_risks.mitigation: Adopt best‑practice storage site selection, continuous monitoring, and compliance with CCS Network Code safety standards.
gen_risks.evidence: CCS Network Code standardises technical and operational arrangements for CO₂ transport and storage (section 4.6)

gen_risks.description: Complex post‑FID role allocations may create accountability gaps and slow issue resolution.
gen_risks.mitigation: Define a RACI matrix for post‑FID responsibilities, provide training, and conduct regular performance reviews.
gen_risks.evidence: Post‑FID roles and responsibilities... managing cross‑chain delivery risks (section 6.4)

gen_risks.description: Regional political considerations in Wales could affect continued support or introduce additional approvals.
gen_risks.mitigation: Engage Welsh Government early, align with devolved administration priorities, and communicate regional benefits.
gen_risks.evidence: Padeswood is located in North Wales, only capture project not in England (section 2.1.8)

gen_risks.description: Reliance on a grant covering only 50% of capital costs may cause cash‑flow strain if equity is insufficient.
gen_risks.mitigation: Secure additional equity or loan facilities, stage capital drawdown aligned with milestones, and monitor cash flow against budget.
gen_risks.evidence: CIF Grant provides upfront capital support up to 50% of eligible capital costs (section 4.3)

gen_risks.description: Future reduction of subsidy support could make the project financially unviable after the initial period.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop a post‑subsidy business case, explore revenue from CO₂ utilisation, and plan for gradual reduction of grant support.
gen_risks.evidence: future market phases are expected to operate with reduced subsidy support (section 4.7)

gt_risks.description: Revenue Support Agreement (RSA) risk. RSA would be paid to the T&S Company (Eni) in two circumstances: where the network is underutilised, and where users are unavailable to inject CO2 and therefore are not paying user fees. [Financial Case Sec 5.4.1, p.14-15.]
gt_risks.mitigation: Padeswood joining the T&S network will reduce the level of network underutilisation and will therefore reduce RSA payments to the T&SCo.

gt_risks.description: Discontinuation risk for Padeswood: the potential for Padeswood to be unable to continue under the business model contract due to the actions of another party or events outside its control - a large-scale, programme-wide issue (e.g. leakage), a prolonged T&S issue, or external events such as Qualifying Change in Law (QCiL), Qualifying Shutdown Events, or Force Majeure. Projects connected via a spurline can also be exposed to an additional risk if the spurline FID is taken after T&S FID, which is not within the capture project's control. [Financial Case Sec 5.4.2, p.14-15.]
gt_risks.mitigation: The risk of having to make a discontinuation payment to Padeswood is judged to be a remote contingent liability given that it is very unlikely (<1%); spurline-timing risk is treated as a variation of the existing cross-chain risks already protected by the business model.

gt_risks.description: Exchequer funding / Secretary of State direct agreement (SoSDA) risk: LCCC is only liable to make payments to the extent it has received sufficient funds from HMG, creating a risk that Padeswood would have no recourse under its private-law contract with LCCC to obtain payments owed if HMG funding to LCCC were insufficient. [Financial Case Sec 5.4.3, p.14-15.]
gt_risks.mitigation: The Secretary of State will sign a direct agreement with Padeswood (to which LCCC is also party) to fund payments directly where LCCC fails to pay; this does not increase DESNZ's overall liabilities or create a contingent liability, as it is an intragroup transaction.

gt_risks.description: Fraud risk across the CCUS programme's grant and contract payments. [Financial Case Sec 5.4.4, p.14-15.]
gt_risks.mitigation: A CCUS Fraud Management Strategy is being developed specifying the programme's strategic approach to deterrence, prevention, detection, and management of fraud and error, including counter-fraud governance and reporting structures and high-quality fraud risk assessments (FRAs) for the different tranches of the CCUS programme.

gt_risks.description: Financial sensitivities: several contractual terms are 'locked in' at Padeswood FID, but drivers of the financial impact continue to move post-FID - notably the carbon market price (Low ETS series used as the reference price for the extension period) and the opex reopener (higher opex expenditure payments), both of which could result in higher subsidy. Other financial sensitivities have the effect of reducing total subsidy. [Financial Case Sec 5.4.5, p.14-15.]
gt_risks.mitigation: Sensitivity analysis has been conducted to estimate the scale of potential subsidy increase from each driver; offsetting sensitivities are also identified and tracked.

gt_risks.description: Cross-chain and cross-cutting risks. Cross-chain risks are risks the private sector is exposed to through the network but cannot mitigate against - T&S Construction delay, Padeswood Construction Delay, Padeswood Underperformance, T&S Underperformance, and Discontinuation Provisions; Padeswood joining the HyNet cluster increases HMG's exposure to compensation payments should the T&S network fail or become unavailable. Cross-cutting risks - inflation risk, carbon price risk, and OpEx risk - are those which are challenging for the private sector to price or relate to events outside their control. [Financial Case Sec 5.4.6, p.14-15; overlaps in subject matter with the Economic Case's Sec 3.4 Risk Appraisal tables, p.10-11, which quantify the value-for-money impact of the same named risks but are a modelling input rather than a risk-register entry, and are excised from planning text for leakage safety but not scored here.]
gt_risks.mitigation: Risk allocation is designed so that each risk sits with the party best placed to manage it; the business model contracts and Network Code are structured to limit and price cross-chain exposure.
